newsitem.title: USA: USDA close on Sun-Diamond bar decision - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: USDA close on Sun-Diamond bar decision - Glickman.

text.p: WASHINGTON, Sept 27 (Rueter) - Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday that the department will make a decision soon on whether or not to bar Sun-Diamond Growers of California from participating in any USDA domestic feeding programs or export promotion programs.
Calling the issue a "very serious matter," Glickman said the decision will be made by USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service, and that "it is in the mill, and the decision will be made soon."

Sun-Diamond, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, was convicted earlier this week in a federal court on eight criminal counts that included illegal gratuities to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy in 1993 and 1994 and illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry.
The charges arose out of the government's two-year special investigation of former USDA secretary Espy.

Sun-Diamond affiliates have been recipients of millions of dollars of government funds through USDA's Market Promotion Program, and sell commodities to the government for its federal school lunch program and other feeding programs.

Asked how the agency would handle possible indictments of two other huge agribusiness firms -- Archer Daniels Midland Co and Tyson Foods Inc, -- Glickman said USDA would look seriously at the matter, but that convictions are the key.

ADM is currently under investigation by the Justice Department for antitrust violations and is working on a plea settlment with the government to avoid an indictment. Tyson Foods is under investigation as part of the Espy probe, and sources close to the case said an indictment of the company cannot be ruled out.
"Convictions are the key, not indictments," said Glickman. "If convictions occur, we will exercise our full authority under the law that we are permitted to do so. These are very serious matters."
